repo_map.purpose: Click is a Python library for building command-line interfaces. You compose commands, groups, options and arguments with decorators. It generates help, parses and converts arguments, prompts the user, shows progress bars, and provides shell completion and a test runner.
repo_map.intended_users: Python developers who write CLI tools. Libraries such as Flask build on it. Pallets maintainers and contributors are the other group.

repo_map.execution_flow: The user calls the command object, or Command.main(), which is core.py:1483. main() takes args from sys.argv[1:], expanding them on Windows, and detects the program name. self._main_shell_completion handles any completion request and exits early. Then make_context builds a Context and calls Command.parse_args, which uses the parser and each Parameter's handle_parse_result. That step resolves the value from the command line, an environment variable, a default map or the default, then runs process_value to convert and validate it. Command.invoke runs the callback. A Group.invoke resolves the subcommand through resolve_command, makes a sub-context and invokes it. In standalone mode, main() catches Exit, Abort, KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError, ClickException and EPIPE OSError. It prints the message and calls sys.exit. With standalone_mode=False it returns the value or propagates the exception.
repo_map.test_runner: pytest. Config is in pyproject.toml: testpaths=tests, filterwarnings=error, and stress tests excluded by default via addopts.
test_conventions: Files are named test_<topic>.py. Larger areas become packages: tests/test_types, tests/test_utils and tests/test_exceptions, with one file per class or function, e.g. test_Choice.py.

compatibility_rules.claim: The public API is whatever src/click/__init__.py re-exports with `as` aliases. Internals use underscore prefixes (_compat, _termui_impl, _utils, _winconsole).
Deprecations keep the old name alive through a module-level __getattr__. It emits DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=2 and a message naming the removal version (Click 9.0, or 9.1 for __version__).
The Python floor is 3.10, and the type checkers target 3.10.
Warnings fail the tests, and stress tests are excluded by default.
Typing is strict. The package ships py.typed (src/click/py.typed). mypy runs in strict mode on src and tests/typing, and pyright runs --verifytypes.
The ruff config requires `typing` imported as `t` and single-line imports.
Docstrings carry versionchanged and versionadded notes. CHANGES.md uses a per-version bullet list with {pr} and {issue} references.
Contributor rules: avoid ternary expressions because coverage cannot measure both branches. Avoid unnecessary dependencies, preferring the standard library. Wrap Markdown at 80 columns.

cards.summary: src/click/core.py holds click's runtime. Context carries per-invocation state and is inherited from the parent context. Command parses args into a context and invokes its callback. Group dispatches to subcommands, with an optional chain mode and a result callback. CommandCollection flattens commands from other groups. Parameter, Option and Argument turn user input into values. Parameter.consume_value picks the value in the order command line, env var, default_map, default. Parameter.process_value then runs type cast, required check and callback. Option adds flags, prompts, counts and auto env vars. ParameterSource is an IntEnum recording where each value came from. A private sentinel, UNSET, marks "no value" internally and is turned into None before user code sees it. Several parameters can share one name (feature switches), and handle_parse_result decides which one wins using ParameterSource.

interfaces.name: ParameterSource
interfaces.behavior: IntEnum with members PROMPT, COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT_MAP, DEFAULT, auto-numbered from most to least explicit. Comparisons such as `source < ParameterSource.DEFAULT_MAP` mean 'explicitly provided'. Parameter.handle_parse_result uses that comparison for deprecation warnings and for feature-switch arbitration.
edge_cases: Context.get_parameter_source returns None for a name that never had a source set
interfaces.signature: class ParameterSource(enum.IntEnum)

interfaces.name: Context.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Builds a context. Most settings (obj, default_map, terminal_width, max_content_width, help_option_names, token_normalize_func, color, show_default) are inherited from the parent when None. allow_extra_args, allow_interspersed_args and ignore_unknown_options fall back to the command's attributes. default_map for a child is parent.default_map.get(info_name) when not given. auto_envvar_prefix is uppercased, and when absent it becomes '<PARENT_PREFIX>_<INFO_NAME upper>'; '-' is replaced by '_'. help_option_names defaults to ['--help']. obj and meta are shared with the parent.
edge_cases: The parent's _opt_prefixes set is copied
an explicit auto_envvar_prefix is uppercased
info_name None means no prefix is derived from the parent

interfaces.name: Context.scope
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that pushes the context onto the thread-local stack. With cleanup=False the depth is bumped so closing callbacks do not run on exit. Context.__enter__ and __exit__ track nesting depth, and only at depth 0 do they run the ExitStack.
edge_cases: Nested entries defer cleanup until the outermost exit
the exit stack is replaced with a new one after closing, so the context can be reused
interfaces.signature: def scope(self, cleanup: bool=True) -> cabc.Generator[Context]

interfaces.name: Context.with_resource
interfaces.behavior: Enters a context manager on the context's ExitStack and returns its __enter__ result. It is cleaned up when the context closes.
interfaces.signature: def with_resource(self, context_manager: AbstractContextManager[V]) -> V

interfaces.name: Context.call_on_close
interfaces.behavior: Registers a callback on the ExitStack, run at teardown in LIFO order. Returns the callback, so it works as a decorator.
interfaces.signature: def call_on_close(self, f: t.Callable[..., t.Any]) -> t.Callable[..., t.Any]

interfaces.name: Context.lookup_default
interfaces.behavior: Reads default_map[name]. Returns None when the map is None, the key is missing, or the stored value is the UNSET sentinel. A callable value is called unless call=False.
edge_cases: a key present with value None counts as 'present' in _default_map_has, so it blocks the parameter's own default
interfaces.signature: def lookup_default(self, name: str, call: bool=True) -> t.Any | None

interfaces.name: Context.invoke
interfaces.behavior: Given a plain callable, runs it with the given args inside `with augment_usage_errors(self), ctx`. Given a Command, it creates a sub-context and, for each exposed param not in kwargs, fills in param.get_default(ctx) cast by type_cast_value (UNSET becomes None). It then stores kwargs in ctx.params and calls the command's callback directly. The command's own parse step and callback chain are skipped.
edge_cases: a Command with callback None raises TypeError
UNSET defaults become None
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, callback: Command | t.Callable[..., V], /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Any | V

interfaces.name: Context.forward
interfaces.behavior: Like invoke, but kwargs missing from the call are filled from the current ctx.params. Only accepts Command objects.
edge_cases: a non-Command argument raises TypeError
interfaces.signature: def forward(self, cmd: Command, /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Context.get_parameter_source
interfaces.behavior: Returns the ParameterSource recorded for the parameter name, or None. Context.set_parameter_source stores it.
edge_cases: unknown name returns None
interfaces.signature: def get_parameter_source(self, name: str) -> ParameterSource | None

interfaces.name: Context.fail
interfaces.behavior: Raises UsageError(message, ctx). Context.abort raises Abort. Context.exit(code=0) first closes the context (running close callbacks), then raises Exit(code).
interfaces.signature: def fail(self, message: str) -> t.NoReturn

interfaces.name: Context.find_object
interfaces.behavior: Walks up the parent chain and returns the first ctx.obj that is an instance of the type, else None. Context.ensure_object does the same, but when none is found it sets self.obj to object_type() and returns that.
edge_cases: ensure_object assigns on the innermost context only
interfaces.signature: def find_object(self, object_type: type[V]) -> V | None

interfaces.name: Command.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Stores name, context_settings (default {}), callback, params (default []), help, epilog, short_help, options_metavar ('[OPTIONS]'), add_help_option, no_args_is_help, hidden and deprecated. Class attributes control context creation: context_class, allow_extra_args=False, allow_interspersed_args=True, ignore_unknown_options=False.
edge_cases: name may be None
params is copied only when falsy, otherwise the same list is stored

interfaces.name: Command.get_params
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.params plus the cached help option when enabled. Under __debug__ it warns (UserWarning) on duplicate option strings. It also warns when a name collides with the reserved help storage name, or when an Argument shares a name with another parameter.
edge_cases: help option names already used by other params are dropped
help option is stored under the reserved name _click_default_help
interfaces.signature: def get_params(self, ctx: Context) -> list[Parameter]

interfaces.name: Command.make_context
interfaces.behavior: Merges context_settings into **extra (explicit extra wins). It builds ctx = self.context_class(self, info_name=..., parent=..., **extra). It then calls parse_args(ctx, args) inside ctx.scope(cleanup=False) and returns the context. It does not invoke the callback.
interfaces.signature: def make_context(self, info_name: str | None, args: list[str], parent: Context | None=None, **extra: t.Any) -> Context

interfaces.name: Command.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Raises NoArgsIsHelpError if there are no args, no_args_is_help is set and parsing is not resilient. It builds the parser with make_parser, parses, then runs handle_parse_result for each param in the order given by iter_params_for_processing (eager first, then the order given on the command line, then declaration order). Remaining UNSET values in ctx.params become None. Extra args raise through ctx.fail unless allow_extra_args or resilient_parsing is set. It then sets ctx.args and merges the option prefixes.
edge_cases: resilient_parsing suppresses the errors
interfaces.signature: def parse_args(self, ctx: Context, args: list[str]) -> list[str]

interfaces.name: Command.invoke
interfaces.behavior: If deprecated, echoes a red 'DeprecationWarning: The command ... is deprecated.' to stderr. If a callback exists, it returns ctx.invoke(self.callback, **ctx.params). With no callback it returns None.
edge_cases: a missing callback returns None silently
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Command.main
interfaces.behavior: Entry point. It reads sys.argv[1:] when args is None (with Windows glob expansion), detects the program name, and handles shell completion through the _<PROG>_COMPLETE env var (exits early). Then it runs make_context and invoke. In standalone mode it calls sys.exit: Exit gives the code, Abort and KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError print 'Aborted!' with exit code 1, ClickException is shown with its exit_code, and EPIPE is silenced. With standalone_mode=False the return value is returned, Exit returns its exit_code, ClickException and Abort propagate, and Ctrl-C/EOF are re-raised as Abort. Command.__call__ is an alias.
edge_cases: a non-EPIPE OSError is re-raised
**extra goes to the Context constructor
interfaces.signature: def main(self, args: cabc.Sequence[str] | None=None, prog_name: str | None=None, complete_var: str | None=None, standalone_mode: bool=True, windows_expand_args: bool=True, **extra: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Command.shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Completes option names when the incomplete token starts with a non-alphanumeric character. It skips hidden options and non-multiple options already given on the command line. It also adds sibling subcommands of any ancestor group that is in chain mode.
interfaces.signature: def shell_complete(self, ctx: Context, incomplete: str) -> list[CompletionItem]

interfaces.name: Group.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Accepts commands as a mapping or a sequence of Commands (a sequence is keyed by c.name, skipping None names). no_args_is_help defaults to `not invoke_without_command`. subcommand_metavar is derived from chain and invoke_without_command. result_callback is stored as _result_callback. It sets allow_extra_args=True and allow_interspersed_args=False at class level, and class-level command_class and group_class attributes.
edge_cases: a chained group with an optional Argument raises RuntimeError

interfaces.name: Group.add_command
interfaces.behavior: Registers cmd under name or cmd.name. In chain mode, adding a Group is rejected through _check_nested_chain.
edge_cases: no name raises TypeError
replaces an existing entry silently
interfaces.signature: def add_command(self, cmd: Command, name: str | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: Group.command
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that builds a command with click.command and registers it on this group. It works with or without parentheses. It uses command_class as cls when no cls kwarg is given.
edge_cases: a bare callable plus kwargs trips an assert
interfaces.signature: def command(self, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[..., t.Any]], Command] | Command

interfaces.name: Group.group
interfaces.behavior: Same as Group.command but for subgroups. group_class is used as cls, and group_class = type means 'use type(self)'.
interfaces.signature: def group(self, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[..., t.Any]], Group] | Group

interfaces.name: Group.result_callback
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that sets the result callback, called as f(result, **group_params). If one already exists, the new one is chained after the old one (old is called first, its result goes to the new one). replace=True overwrites the old one. The callback receives a single return value, or a list of return values in chain mode.
edge_cases: a group with invoke_without_command and no subcommand passes the group's return value, or [] in chain mode
interfaces.signature: def result_callback(self, replace: bool=False) -> t.Callable[[F], F]

interfaces.name: Group.invoke
interfaces.behavior: With no subcommand: if invoke_without_command is set it runs the group callback and then the result callback, otherwise it fails with 'Missing command.'. In normal mode it resolves the command, sets ctx.invoked_subcommand, runs the group callback, builds the subcontext and invokes it. In chain mode it sets invoked_subcommand to '*' (or None when there are no args), runs the group callback, then builds all subcontexts first (allow_extra_args=True, allow_interspersed_args=False) and invokes them in order, collecting the results in a list. Both modes feed the result callback.
edge_cases: the group callback runs before the subcommand is parsed
in chain mode all subcommand parsing completes before any subcommand runs
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Group.resolve_command
interfaces.behavior: Looks up args[0] with get_command. On a miss it retries after token_normalize_func. If the token still misses and parsing is not resilient and it looks like an option, it re-runs self.parse_args(ctx, args), so --help and errors on group options surface. Otherwise it raises NoSuchCommand with the possibilities. Returns (name, cmd, rest).
edge_cases: with resilient_parsing it returns (None, None, rest)
interfaces.signature: def resolve_command(self, ctx: Context, args: list[str]) -> tuple[str | None, Command | None, list[str]]

interfaces.name: Group.get_command
interfaces.behavior: Plain lookup in self.commands. list_commands returns sorted(self.commands). Both are the overridable hooks for dynamic or lazy command loading, and help, completion, to_info_dict and resolve_command all go through them.
edge_cases: help skips commands for which get_command returns None
interfaces.signature: def get_command(self, ctx: Context, cmd_name: str) -> Command | None

interfaces.name: CommandCollection
interfaces.behavior: A Group subclass with a list of sources (Groups). get_command checks its own commands first, then each source in order. list_commands is the sorted union. Source parameters and callbacks are not used. add_source appends a source. In chain mode a source Group raises RuntimeError.
edge_cases: first source wins on a name collision
interfaces.signature: class CommandCollection(Group)  # __init__(self, name: str | None=None, sources: list[Group] | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any)

interfaces.name: Parameter.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Parses the declarations with _parse_decls. It resolves the type via types.convert_type(type, default), and nargs defaults to the composite type's arity or 1. default defaults to the UNSET sentinel, and _default_explicit records whether a default was passed. If deprecated is set, a '(DEPRECATED...)' label is appended to help. The ValueError checks run only under __debug__.
edge_cases: a composite type with a mismatched nargs raises ValueError
required together with deprecated raises ValueError

interfaces.name: Parameter.consume_value
interfaces.behavior: Resolves the raw value in precedence order. First the parser value (COMMANDLINE), then the envvar via value_from_envvar (ENVIRONMENT), then ctx.lookup_default (DEFAULT_MAP; a string is split when nargs != 1), then get_default (DEFAULT). It returns (value, source) and gives UNSET if nothing is found.
edge_cases: an empty envvar string counts as unset
a default_map key present with None is used as the value
interfaces.signature: def consume_value(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, t.Any]) -> tuple[t.Any, ParameterSource]

interfaces.name: Parameter.type_cast_value
interfaces.behavior: None becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise it stays None. It converts via self.type, per item for nargs=-1, as an exact-length tuple for nargs>1, and wraps in a tuple per item for multiple.
edge_cases: a non-iterable value raises BadParameter 'Value must be an iterable.'
a nargs length mismatch raises BadParameter 'Takes N values but M were given.'
interfaces.signature: def type_cast_value(self, ctx: Context, value: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Parameter.process_value
interfaces.behavior: UNSET becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise the value is type cast. A required parameter whose value is missing raises MissingParameter. The callback(ctx, param, value) then runs. It receives None for UNSET, and while it runs, other UNSET entries in ctx.params are shown as None.
edge_cases: value_is_missing treats UNSET and () (for nargs != 1 or multiple) as missing
interfaces.signature: def process_value(self, ctx: Context, value: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Parameter.handle_parse_result
interfaces.behavior: Per-parameter pipeline. It calls consume_value, records the source, echoes a red deprecation warning to stderr if the value is explicit (source < DEFAULT_MAP), then process_value. In resilient_parsing mode any exception turns the value into UNSET. It then decides which parameter owns ctx.params[name] when several share a name (feature switches): a more explicit source wins, and the same source wins by later order unless that would replace an explicit default with an inferred one. It writes ctx.params only if expose_value is true.
edge_cases: errors are wrapped in augment_usage_errors, which attaches ctx and param to BadParameter
interfaces.signature: def handle_parse_result(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, t.Any], args: list[str]) -> tuple[t.Any, list[str]]

interfaces.name: Option.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Steps in order: prompt text (prompt=True needs a name and becomes the name with underscores replaced by spaces, capitalised); flag inference; type picking (count gives IntRange(min=0); bool flag gives BoolParamType); count sets default=0 if default was unset; then validation. is_flag is inferred from flag_value, secondary '/' declarations, or an explicit value. Option.get_default lazily resolves UNSET to False for non-required boolean flags, () for non-required multi flags, and True to flag_value for non-boolean flags.
edge_cases: prompt=True without a name raises TypeError
deprecated with prompt raises ValueError
nargs=-1 raises TypeError
secondary opts on a non-bool flag raise TypeError
count with multiple or is_flag raises TypeError
a repeated name, an identical true/false pair, or no derivable name raise TypeError/ValueError
a name given without any option strings raises TypeError

interfaces.name: Option.consume_value
interfaces.behavior: Extends Parameter.consume_value. If the parser yielded FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE, it prompts when prompt is set and parsing is not resilient (source PROMPT), otherwise it uses flag_activation_value (COMMANDLINE). It also substitutes the activation value inside multiple lists. When the value is unset or comes from a default, and prompt is enabled with (required or prompt_required), it calls prompt_for_value (source PROMPT).

interfaces.signature: def consume_value(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, Parameter]) -> tuple[t.Any, ParameterSource]

interfaces.name: Option.value_from_envvar
interfaces.behavior: Uses Parameter.resolve_envvar_value, then falls back to '<ctx.auto_envvar_prefix>_<NAME>' when allow_from_autoenv is true. For non-bool flags: the string equal to flag_value gives flag_value; a truthy bool reading gives flag_value, a falsy one gives False, and an unrecognised one gives None. Otherwise it splits for nargs != 1 or multiple (batched by nargs when both apply).
edge_cases: empty env value counts as unset
interfaces.signature: def value_from_envvar(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Option.prompt_for_value
interfaces.behavior: Locks in get_default, then uses confirm() for boolean flags (default coerced to bool, or None when unset). Otherwise it calls prompt() with type, hide_input, confirmation_prompt, show_choices, and value_proc=process_value.
edge_cases: show_default is forwarded only when not None
interfaces.signature: def prompt_for_value(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Argument.__init__
interfaces.behavior: required defaults to True when no default was given and nargs > 0 (nargs=-1 gives False), and to False when a default exists. multiple is rejected. Exactly one declaration is allowed, and the name is the declaration with '-' replaced by '_' and lower-cased. param_type_name is 'argument'. A deprecated argument gets '!' appended to its metavar. Optional arguments are shown in [brackets] unless the metavar is already bracketed, and nargs != 1 appends '...'.
edge_cases: multiple raises TypeError
no declaration with expose_value=True raises TypeError
more than one declaration raises TypeError
no declaration with expose_value=False gives an empty name
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, param_decls: cabc.Sequence[str], required: bool | None=None, help: str | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> None

cards.error_conventions: Programming errors use built-in exceptions: TypeError for bad declarations (names, flag/prompt/count combinations, Argument with multiple or the wrong number of decls, missing command name or callback); ValueError for invalid combinations such as required+deprecated, deprecated+prompt, nargs vs composite type arity, or a same-flag true/false pair; RuntimeError for chain-mode misuse (nested groups, optional arguments in chain mode). Many of these checks run only under __debug__ (Parameter.__init__, Option._validate). Messages are plain, with quoted names (e.g. "'nargs' must be ..."). Runtime user errors use click.exceptions: UsageError (via ctx.fail, e.g. 'Missing command.' and 'Got unexpected extra argument(s) (...)'), BadParameter (conversion, 'Takes N values but M were given.', 'Value must be an iterable.'), MissingParameter, NoSuchCommand, NoArgsIsHelpError. Exit and Abort are control flow. The augment_usage_errors context manager attaches ctx and param to errors that lack them. User-facing strings go through gettext (`_`, ngettext); developer errors do not. Deprecation notices are echoed in red to stderr as 'DeprecationWarning: The ... is deprecated.[ reason]'. Python warnings.warn is used for duplicate names/opts (in Command.get_params) and for deprecated attribute access (BaseCommand, MultiCommand, Context.protected_args).

gaps.description: No built-in command aliases or unambiguous-prefix matching for subcommands. Group.resolve_command does exact lookup, plus token_normalize_func, only.
gaps.why_plausible: A small override or hook in resolve_command would cover it. Documented recipes for this exist but nothing in core.

gaps.description: No mutually-exclusive or required-together option constraints. Options only interact through shared names (feature switches).
gaps.why_plausible: The post-parse pass in Command.parse_args has all params and sources available, so a validation hook could slot in there.

gaps.description: No built-in config-file or layered default source. default_map is the only injection point and must be supplied by the caller.
gaps.why_plausible: consume_value already has an ordered source chain, so another source would fit between ENVIRONMENT and DEFAULT_MAP, with a matching ParameterSource member.

gaps.description: No per-command post-parse or pre-invoke hooks. Only Group.result_callback exists, and only for groups.
gaps.why_plausible: Command.invoke is a single place to wrap, and the Group result-callback chaining logic could be reused.

gaps.description: Group.add_command silently overwrites existing names, and there is no way to remove or unregister a command.
gaps.why_plausible: It is a small API addition, and commands is a plain dict.

gaps.description: Option has no explicit group or section for help output. Command.format_options lists all options in one flat section.
gaps.why_plausible: Option.get_help_record and Command.format_options are the natural place for grouping.

limitations: Environment variables are always strings and are split via type.split_envvar_value for nargs != 1. An empty env var counts as unset.
Options do not support nargs=-1 (TypeError), and Arguments do not support multiple.
Chain-mode groups cannot contain nested Groups or optional Arguments (RuntimeError).
A default_map key that is present with value None blocks the parameter's own default.
Many constructor validations run only under __debug__, so `python -O` skips them.
The UNSET sentinel is internal. User code, callbacks and invoke() see None, but Option.default keeps the raw UNSET.
Several methods (consume_value, process_value, handle_parse_result, resolve_envvar_value) are :meta private: and may change.
Duplicate-option detection only warns, and only in debug mode.
Context.protected_args, BaseCommand and MultiCommand are deprecated, with warnings.
In chain mode every subcommand is parsed before any runs, and ctx.invoked_subcommand is only '*'.

cards.summary: src/click/decorators.py (626 lines) holds the decorator layer. Context-passing decorators: pass_context, pass_obj, make_pass_decorator, pass_meta_key. Builders: command and group. Parameter attachers: argument and option. Pre-configured options: confirmation_option, password_option, version_option, custom_version_option and help_option. Parameters are stashed on the function's `__click_params__` list by `_param_memo`. `command()` consumes that list when it builds the Command, and it appends in reverse so the order matches the source. All pre-configured options are thin wrappers that call `option()` with `kwargs.setdefault(...)`.

interfaces.name: pass_context
interfaces.behavior: Wraps f so it is called with get_current_context() as first arg, then the original args. Uses update_wrapper. Does not go through ctx.invoke.
edge_cases: Called outside an active context, get_current_context() raises RuntimeError (raised in globals, not here)
interfaces.signature: def pass_context(f: t.Callable[te.Concatenate[Context, P], R]) -> t.Callable[P, R]

interfaces.name: pass_obj
interfaces.behavior: Passes get_current_context().obj as first arg, then the original args. Uses update_wrapper.
edge_cases: obj may be None if the context has no obj set; it is passed through as None
interfaces.signature: def pass_obj(f: t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]) -> t.Callable[P, R]

interfaces.name: make_pass_decorator
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator. At call time it takes ctx.ensure_object(object_type) if ensure=True, otherwise ctx.find_object(object_type). It then calls ctx.invoke(f, obj, *args, **kwargs).
edge_cases: With ensure=False and no matching object found (None), it raises RuntimeError
ensure=True creates the object and stores it on the context
Uses isinstance matching via find_object, over the innermost context outward
interfaces.signature: def make_pass_decorator(object_type: type[T], ensure: bool=False) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]], t.Callable[P, R]]

interfaces.name: pass_meta_key
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator that passes ctx.meta[key] as first arg via ctx.invoke. Builds the decorator's __doc__ from doc_description, defaulting to "the 'key' key from :attr:`click.Context.meta`". doc_description is keyword-only.
edge_cases: A missing key raises KeyError from ctx.meta[key] at call time
interfaces.signature: def pass_meta_key(key: str, *, doc_description: str | None=None) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]], t.Callable[P, R]]

interfaces.name: command
interfaces.behavior: Creates a Command (or `cls`) from a function. Usable bare (`@command`) or with parentheses. If `name` is callable it is treated as the function, and cls/attrs must be unset, enforced with assert. The decorator pops `params` from attrs. It appends the function's `__click_params__` in reversed order and deletes the attribute. help defaults to f.__doc__ when attrs['help'] is None. The name defaults to f.__name__ lowercased with _ replaced by -, and a trailing -command/-cmd/-group/-grp suffix is stripped. It then builds cls(name=..., callback=f, params=params, **attrs) and sets cmd.__doc__ = f.__doc__.
edge_cases: Decorating an existing Command raises TypeError
`attrs.pop('params')` mutates the shared attrs dict, so a decorator object reused across several functions loses `params` after its first use
The caller's params list is extended in place
A name that is only a suffix (e.g. 'command') is not stripped, because rpartition finds no separator
A positional name passed together with a callable name is not allowed (assert)
interfaces.signature: def command(name: str | _AnyCallable | None=None, cls: type[CmdType] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> Command | t.Callable[[_AnyCallable], Command | CmdType]

interfaces.name: group
interfaces.behavior: Same as command, with cls defaulting to Group. A callable `name` gives command(cls=cls, **attrs)(name). Otherwise it calls command(name, cls, **attrs).
edge_cases: With bare use, a positional cls is not possible (name is the function)
interfaces.signature: def group(name: str | _AnyCallable | None=None, cls: type[GrpType] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> Group | t.Callable[[_AnyCallable], Group | GrpType]

interfaces.name: argument
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator that builds cls(param_decls, **attrs), with cls defaulting to Argument. It attaches it through _param_memo and returns f unchanged.
edge_cases: Works on a Command instance, where it appends directly to f.params (not reversed), or on a plain function, where it appends to __click_params__
Decorator order: the bottom-most decorator becomes the first parameter, because command() reverses the list
interfaces.signature: def argument(*param_decls: str, cls: type[Argument] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: option
interfaces.behavior: Same as argument but builds an Option, with cls defaulting to Option. param_decls are passed as a tuple to the constructor. Attaches it via _param_memo and returns f.
edge_cases: The Option is instantiated when the decorator is applied, not at decoration-factory time, so each application gets a fresh Option
Declaration errors come from Option.__init__ (core)
interfaces.signature: def option(*param_decls: str, cls: type[Option] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: confirmation_option
interfaces.behavior: Wraps option. Default decl is ('--yes'). Defaults set with setdefault: is_flag=True, callback (calls ctx.abort() if the value is falsy), expose_value=False, prompt=_('Do you want to continue?'), help=_('Confirm the action without prompting.').
edge_cases: Any default can be overridden through kwargs
Declining the prompt aborts, so Abort/exit code 1
Passing --yes skips the prompt
interfaces.signature: def confirmation_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: password_option
interfaces.behavior: Wraps option. Default decl is ('--password'). Defaults set with setdefault: prompt=True, confirmation_prompt=True, hide_input=True. The value stays exposed to the function.
edge_cases: The values can be overridden in kwargs
interfaces.signature: def password_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: version_option
interfaces.behavior: Adds an eager --version flag. Signature: (version=None, *param_decls, package_name=None, prog_name=None, message=None, **kwargs). If both version and package_name are None, it inspects the caller's frame globals (__name__, or __package__ if __main__) and takes the top-level segment as package_name. The callback is skipped if the value is falsy or ctx.resilient_parsing. prog_name defaults to ctx.find_root().info_name. If version is None, it calls importlib.metadata.version(package_name). On PackageNotFoundError it tries packages_distributions(): one match is used, several raise RuntimeError, none raise RuntimeError. The default message is '%(prog)s, version %(version)s', and the % mapping has only prog, package and version. It then echoes with color=ctx.color and calls ctx.exit(). Defaults set with setdefault: is_flag, expose_value=False, is_eager=True, help. callback is forced via kwargs['callback'] = callback, which overrides any user callback.
edge_cases: Version detection is lazy (done at invocation, not at decoration time)
Caches the resolved version, prog_name and package_name through nonlocal
If version is None and package_name is None and the frame cannot be found, a RuntimeError is raised at invocation
The docstring says the message slots are frozen
interfaces.signature: def version_option(version: str | None=None, *param_decls: str, package_name: str | None=None, prog_name: str | None=None, message: str | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: custom_version_option
interfaces.behavior: Added in 8.5.0. Signature: (callback: Callable[[Context], str], *param_decls, **kwargs). The inner show_version skips when the value is falsy or ctx.resilient_parsing. Otherwise it echoes callback(ctx) with color=ctx.color and calls ctx.exit(). Default decl is ('--version'). Defaults set with setdefault: is_flag, expose_value=False, is_eager=True, help. callback is forced via kwargs['callback'] = show_version.
edge_cases: The user's callback receives only a Context
Passing callback= in kwargs would conflict with the positional parameter name; use the positional parameter instead
interfaces.signature: def custom_version_option(callback: t.Callable[[Context], str], *param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: help_option
interfaces.behavior: Adds a --help flag. Default decl is ('--help'). The callback show_help echoes ctx.get_help() with color=ctx.color and calls ctx.exit(), when the value is set and not resilient_parsing. Defaults set with setdefault: is_flag, expose_value=False, is_eager=True, help=_('Show this message and exit.'), callback=show_help.
edge_cases: The callback can be overridden through kwargs
Passing custom names, e.g. '-h', is the supported way to rename help flags
interfaces.signature: def help_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

cards.error_conventions: TypeError is used for double conversion of a callback into a command (message: 'Attempted to convert a callback into a command twice.'). AssertionError is used with imperative 'Use ...' messages for misuse of the bare form of command. RuntimeError is used at invocation time for missing context objects (make_pass_decorator) and for version detection failures; the message quotes the name with !r and suggests passing 'package_name'. User-facing option strings are wrapped in gettext `_()`. Failures are not raised as ClickException.

gaps.description: There is no pass-decorator for a named key of ctx.params or ctx.obj attribute, and no option-less decorator for other eager options (e.g. --debug or --verbose counting flags).

gaps.description: version_option replaces any user-supplied `callback` (kwargs['callback'] = callback), unlike help_option and confirmation_option, which use setdefault. Its message slots are documented as frozen.

gaps.description: Missing-key errors from pass_meta_key surface as a bare KeyError, with no message naming the key.

cards.summary: src/click/types.py defines ParamType, a generic abstract base class. A ParamType validates and converts a raw value (CLI string, env var, default or prompt input) into a Python value. Its subclasses are FuncParamType, UnprocessedParamType, StringParamType, Choice, DateTime, IntParamType/IntRange, FloatParamType/FloatRange, BoolParamType, UUIDParameterType, File, Path and the composite Tuple. convert_type maps Python types or defaults to ParamType instances. Module-level singletons are UNPROCESSED, STRING, INT, FLOAT, BOOL and UUID. Failures go through ParamType.fail, which raises BadParameter. Every type has to_info_dict for documentation tooling. A few types add shell_complete and get_metavar. I read the whole file. For tests I read only test_Choice.py in full, and I grepped test_convert_type.py and test_info_dict.py. I did not read the docs.

interfaces.name: ParamType
interfaces.behavior: Generic ABC (value type, input type). Class attrs: is_composite=False, arity=1, name (must be set by subclasses), envvar_list_splitter=None (None means whitespace split). The default convert returns the value unchanged. On Python < 3.13, __class_getitem__ fills in Any as the second type parameter.
edge_cases: A subclass without `name` gets the class name (suffix stripped) in to_info_dict via hasattr
interfaces.signature: class ParamType(t.Generic[_ValueT_co, _InputT_contra], abc.ABC)

interfaces.name: ParamType.__call__
interfaces.behavior: Returns None if value is None. Otherwise returns self.convert(value, param, ctx). param and ctx default to None.
edge_cases: None short-circuits without calling convert
interfaces.signature: def __call__(self, value: _InputT_contra | None, param: Parameter | None=None, ctx: Context | None=None) -> _ValueT_co | None

interfaces.name: ParamType.convert
interfaces.behavior: Override point. The base implementation returns the value as-is (cast). Subclasses should accept already-converted values and work with param and ctx set to None (prompts).
edge_cases: param/ctx may be None
interfaces.signature: def convert(self, value: _InputT_contra, param: Parameter | None, ctx: Context | None) -> _ValueT_co

interfaces.name: ParamType.fail
interfaces.behavior: Raises BadParameter(message, ctx=ctx, param=param). Typed NoReturn.
interfaces.signature: def fail(self, message: str, param: Parameter | None=None, ctx: Context | None=None) -> t.NoReturn

interfaces.name: ParamType.to_info_dict
interfaces.behavior: Returns {'param_type': class name truncated at 'ParamType' and then 'ParameterType', 'name': self.name or the class-derived name}. Subclasses extend it by merging extra keys.
edge_cases: IntParamType gives 'Int', UUIDParameterType gives 'UUID'
interfaces.signature: def to_info_dict(self) -> ParamTypeInfoDict

interfaces.name: ParamType.get_metavar
interfaces.behavior: Returns None by default. Used for help-text metavar.
interfaces.signature: def get_metavar(self, param: Parameter, ctx: Context) -> str | None

interfaces.name: ParamType.get_missing_message
interfaces.behavior: Returns None by default. Extra text for a missing-parameter error.
interfaces.signature: def get_missing_message(self, param: Parameter, ctx: Context | None) -> str | None

interfaces.name: ParamType.split_envvar_value
interfaces.behavior: Returns (rv or '').split(self.envvar_list_splitter).
edge_cases: None or empty string becomes ''.split(), which is []
With a splitter of None, whitespace is stripped; otherwise empty items can appear
interfaces.signature: def split_envvar_value(self, rv: str) -> cabc.Sequence[str]

interfaces.name: ParamType.shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Returns [] by default. Subclasses return CompletionItem lists.
interfaces.signature: def shell_complete(self, ctx: Context, param: Parameter, incomplete: str) -> list[CompletionItem]

interfaces.name: CompositeParamType
interfaces.behavior: ParamType subclass with is_composite=True and an abstract arity property. Base for Tuple.
interfaces.signature: class CompositeParamType(ParamType[_ValueT_co])

interfaces.name: FuncParamType
interfaces.behavior: Wraps a callable. name is func.__name__. convert calls func(value). A ValueError becomes fail(str(exc)). If the message is empty it falls back to str(value), or to bytes decoded as utf-8 with 'replace' on UnicodeError. to_info_dict adds 'func'.
edge_cases: Only ValueError is caught; other exceptions propagate
Callables without __name__ (e.g. functools.partial) fail in __init__ with AttributeError
interfaces.signature: class FuncParamType(ParamType[_ValueT_co], t.Generic[_ValueT_contra, _ValueT_co])  # __init__(self, func: t.Callable[[_ValueT_contra], _ValueT_co])

interfaces.name: UnprocessedParamType
interfaces.behavior: name='text'. convert returns the value untouched, so bytes are not decoded. repr is 'UNPROCESSED'.
interfaces.signature: class UnprocessedParamType(ParamType[t.Any])

interfaces.name: StringParamType
interfaces.behavior: name='text'. bytes are decoded with the argv encoding, then the filesystem encoding, then utf-8 with 'replace'. Anything else becomes str(value).
edge_cases: Never fails; undecodable bytes get replacement characters
interfaces.signature: class StringParamType(ParamType[str])

interfaces.name: Choice
interfaces.behavior: Choice(choices, case_sensitive=True). choices is stored as a tuple, so any iterable works. convert normalizes the input and each choice via normalize_choice, then returns the first original choice whose normalized form matches. Enum members normalize to .name, other values to str(). If ctx.token_normalize_func is set it is applied. With case_sensitive=False the value is casefolded. get_metavar gives {a|b} for a required argument and [a|b] otherwise. For an option with show_choices False it shows type names, e.g. [TEXT]. get_missing_message lists the choices. shell_complete returns prefix-matching CompletionItems. to_info_dict adds choices and case_sensitive.
edge_cases: The mapping is rebuilt on every convert call
Duplicate normalized values silently resolve to the first match
Non-str inputs are normalized with str()
interfaces.signature: class Choice(ParamType[_ValueT_co], t.Generic[_ValueT_co])  # __init__(self, choices: cabc.Iterable[_ValueT_co], case_sensitive: bool=True)

interfaces.name: Choice.normalize_choice
interfaces.behavior: normalize_choice(choice, ctx) -> str. Override to customize how values and choices are mapped to strings. Each choice should normalize to a unique string.
edge_cases: ctx may be None
interfaces.signature: def normalize_choice(self, choice: object, ctx: Context | None) -> str

interfaces.name: Choice.get_invalid_choice_message
interfaces.behavior: get_invalid_choice_message(value, ctx) uses ngettext. Singular: "'d' is not 'a'." Plural: "'d' is not one of 'a', 'b', 'c'." Normalized choices are shown with repr.
edge_cases: The plural form is chosen by len(self.choices)
interfaces.signature: def get_invalid_choice_message(self, value: t.Any, ctx: Context | None) -> str

interfaces.name: DateTime
interfaces.behavior: DateTime(formats=None). Defaults to '%Y-%m-%d', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S' and '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'. convert returns a datetime as-is. Otherwise it tries each format with strptime in order and returns the first success. get_metavar returns [fmt1|fmt2]. to_info_dict adds formats.
edge_cases: An empty formats list falls back to the defaults (`formats or [...]`)
A non-str value passed to strptime raises TypeError, which is not caught
A generator for formats is unsafe
interfaces.signature: class DateTime(ParamType[datetime])  # __init__(self, formats: cabc.Sequence[str] | None=None)

interfaces.name: IntRange
interfaces.behavior: IntRange(min=None, max=None, min_open=False, max_open=False, clamp=False), a subclass of IntParamType. Converts via int() and then checks the range. With clamp, an out-of-range value returns the bound, or bound±1 when that side is open. Otherwise it fails with '{value} is not in the range {x<=...}.' to_info_dict includes min, max, min_open, max_open and clamp. name='integer range'.

int() ValueError becomes 'is not a valid integer range' (the message uses self.name)
interfaces.signature: class IntRange(_NumberRangeBase[int, int], IntParamType)

interfaces.name: FloatRange

edge_cases: float('nan') passes the range comparisons as False and so is accepted
The error message uses the type name, 'float range'

Float strings are rejected
interfaces.signature: class IntParamType(_NumberParamTypeBase[t.SupportsInt | t.SupportsIndex, int])

interfaces.name: FloatParamType

interfaces.signature: class FloatParamType(_NumberParamTypeBase[t.SupportsFloat | t.SupportsIndex, float])

interfaces.name: BoolParamType
interfaces.behavior: name='boolean'. The bool_states dict maps 1/0/yes/no/true/false/on/off/t/f/y/n and '' to a bool. str_to_bool strips and lowercases, and passes through bool values. It returns None for unknown strings, and convert then fails listing the sorted recognized values.
edge_cases: The empty string converts to False
A non-str, non-bool value (e.g. int 1) raises AttributeError on .strip()
interfaces.signature: class BoolParamType(ParamType[bool])

interfaces.name: UUIDParameterType
interfaces.behavior: name='uuid'. Returns a uuid.UUID as-is. Otherwise strips the string and calls uuid.UUID. Exposed as the UUID singleton.
edge_cases: Invalid input fails with "... is not a valid UUID."
interfaces.signature: class UUIDParameterType(ParamType[uuid.UUID])

interfaces.name: File
interfaces.behavior: File(mode='r', encoding=None, errors='strict', lazy=None, atomic=False). Values that already have read or write are returned as-is. resolve_lazy_flag: an explicit lazy wins; '-' is never lazy; a mode containing 'w' is lazy; otherwise not lazy. A lazy file becomes _LazyFile and is registered via ctx.call_on_close(close_intelligently). A non-lazy file is opened with open_stream and closed or flushed on context close. OSError becomes fail with "'filename': strerror". envvar_list_splitter is os.path.pathsep. shell_complete returns a file-type CompletionItem.
edge_cases: With ctx=None the caller must close the file
Modes like 'a' or 'x' are not lazy by default
Only 'w' triggers the lazy default
interfaces.signature: class File(ParamType[t.IO[t.Any]])  # __init__(self, mode: str='r', encoding: str | None=None, errors: str | None='strict', lazy: bool | None=None, atomic: bool=False)

interfaces.name: Path
interfaces.behavior: Path(exists=False, file_okay=True, dir_okay=True, writable=False, readable=True, resolve_path=False, allow_dash=False, path_type=None, executable=False). name is 'file', 'directory' or 'path' depending on file_okay and dir_okay. convert skips checks for '-' when file_okay and allow_dash are set. With resolve_path it applies realpath. If os.stat fails and exists is False it returns the coerced value without further checks. Otherwise it checks existence, then file vs dir, then readable, writable and executable. coerce_path_result applies path_type: str uses fsdecode, bytes uses fsencode, other types are called with the value. The executable check uses the original value, not the resolved rv.
edge_cases: Checks are skipped silently for a nonexistent path when exists=False
Dash with bytes input is compared against b'-'
to_info_dict omits executable, resolve_path and path_type
interfaces.signature: class Path(ParamType[_PathT_co, str | os.PathLike[str]], t.Generic[_PathT_co])  # __init__(self, exists: bool=False, file_okay: bool=True, dir_okay: bool=True, writable: bool=False, readable: bool=True, resolve_path: bool=False, allow_dash: bool=False, path_type: type[_PathT_co] | None=None, executable: bool=False)

interfaces.name: Path.coerce_path_result
interfaces.behavior: coerce_path_result(value) converts to self.type (the path_type argument). It is a no-op when the value is already an instance of that type.
edge_cases: path_type=None leaves the value unchanged
interfaces.signature: def coerce_path_result(self, value: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> _PathT_co

interfaces.name: Tuple
interfaces.behavior: Tuple(types) is a composite type. Each entry goes through convert_type. arity is len(types). name is '<int text>' style. convert checks the length, then applies each type to its item and returns a tuple. to_info_dict nests each type's info dict.
edge_cases: len(value) is called, so a non-sized value raises TypeError
An empty tuple has arity 0
interfaces.signature: class Tuple(CompositeParamType[tuple[t.Any, ...]])  # __init__(self, types: cabc.Sequence[type[t.Any] | ParamType[t.Any]])

interfaces.name: convert_type
interfaces.behavior: convert_type(ty=None, default=None). _guess_type infers the type from the default. A tuple or list default uses its first item's type, or a tuple of types for nested sequences, and an empty one gives STRING. A tuple of types yields Tuple. A ParamType instance is returned unchanged. str or None gives STRING, int gives INT, float gives FLOAT, bool gives BOOL. A guessed type with no match falls back to STRING. Any other callable is wrapped in FuncParamType.
edge_cases: Passing a ParamType subclass instead of an instance fails an AssertionError check when __debug__ is on
dict or list are wrapped as FuncParamType
uuid.UUID is not special-cased and becomes FuncParamType
interfaces.signature: def convert_type(ty: t.Any | None=None, default: t.Any | None=None) -> ParamType[t.Any]

interfaces.name: BoolParamType.str_to_bool
interfaces.behavior: Static method that returns the bool for a string, or None when unknown.
edge_cases: bool input is returned as-is
interfaces.signature: def str_to_bool(value: str | bool) -> bool | None

cards.error_conventions: Conversion and validation failures call ParamType.fail, which raises click.exceptions.BadParameter(message, ctx=ctx, param=param). Programmer errors raise other types: FloatRange.__init__ raises TypeError, FloatRange._clamp raises RuntimeError, and convert_type raises AssertionError when given a ParamType class. Messages are wrapped in gettext `_()`, or ngettext for singular/plural, and use `{value!r}`. Formats include "{value!r} is not a valid integer.", "{value} is not in the range {range}.", "{Name} {filename!r} does not exist." and "{value!r} is not one of 'a', 'b'.". Errors from the OS for File are "'name': strerror".

cards.summary: src/click/parser.py is Click's internal, optparse-derived parser. _OptionParser holds short/long option tables and positional _Argument specs. parse_args first scans options (_process_args_for_options) and then assigns positionals via _unpack_args. It returns (opts dict, leftover args, order list of Parameter objects). Core's Command.make_parser builds it and Option/Argument.add_to_parser register params. Old public names (OptionParser, Option, Argument, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState, split_arg_string) are served by a module __getattr__ that emits DeprecationWarning.

interfaces.name: _OptionParser
interfaces.behavior: Internal parser. __init__(ctx=None) sets allow_interspersed_args=True and ignore_unknown_options=False, then copies both from ctx if given. Maintains _short_opt, _long_opt dicts, _opt_prefixes={'-','--'}, _args list. Docstring marks it deprecated 8.2, removal in 9.0.
edge_cases: ctx None is allowed: no token normalization, no resilient parsing
interfaces.signature: class _OptionParser  # __init__(self, ctx: Context | None=None)

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_option
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes each opt string via _normalize_opt (ctx.token_normalize_func), builds an _Option, adds its prefixes to _opt_prefixes, and registers short opts in _short_opt and long opts in _long_opt. dest is not inferred. Actions: store, store_const, append, append_const, count (default store).
edge_cases: Option string with no prefix (starts with alnum) raises ValueError from _Option
Later registration of the same opt string overwrites the earlier one
Custom prefixes such as + or ! get added to _opt_prefixes
interfaces.signature: def add_option(self, obj: CoreOption, opts: cabc.Sequence[str], dest: str | None, action: str | None=None, nargs: int=1, const: t.Any | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_argument
interfaces.behavior: Appends an _Argument(obj, dest, nargs) to _args. Order of calls determines positional order.
edge_cases: nargs=-1 means consume the remainder; two nargs<0 args later raise TypeError in _unpack_args
interfaces.signature: def add_argument(self, obj: CoreArgument, dest: str | None, nargs: int=1) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Creates _ParsingState(args), runs _process_args_for_options then _process_args_for_args, and returns (state.opts, state.largs, state.order). Mutates the passed list (rargs is popped).
edge_cases: UsageError is swallowed when ctx is not None and ctx.resilient_parsing is True, returning the partial state
Without ctx, UsageError always propagates
interfaces.signature: def parse_args(self, args: list[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, t.Any], list[str], list[CoreParameter]]

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_options
interfaces.behavior: Loop popping from rargs. '--' stops option processing and is consumed (dropped). An arg whose first char is in _opt_prefixes and len>1 goes to _process_opts. Otherwise, with allow_interspersed_args it is appended to largs, else it is pushed back onto rargs and parsing stops.
edge_cases: A lone '-' is treated as a positional
Without interspersed args, the first non-option stops option parsing
interfaces.signature: def _process_args_for_options(self, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_args
interfaces.behavior: Calls _unpack_args on largs+rargs using each arg's nargs, calls each _Argument.process with its slice, then sets largs to the leftovers and rargs to [].
edge_cases: Surplus values stay in largs, which is the returned leftover list
Missing values become UNSET
interfaces.signature: def _process_args_for_args(self, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_opts
interfaces.behavior: Splits arg on the first '=' into long_opt and explicit_value, normalizes, and tries _match_long_opt. On NoSuchOption: if arg[:2] is not a known prefix (for example '-abc'), falls back to _match_short_opt. Otherwise, re-raises unless ignore_unknown_options, in which case the whole arg goes to largs.
edge_cases: '-foo' can match a registered long option with a single dash
Short-option clusters are only tried for single-char prefixes
interfaces.signature: def _process_opts(self, arg: str, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_long_opt
interfaces.behavior: Looks up opt in _long_opt. If the option takes a value, an explicit '=value' is inserted at the front of rargs and then read by _get_value_from_state. Otherwise the value is UNSET, then option.process is called.
edge_cases: Unknown opt raises NoSuchOption with possibilities=_long_opt for suggestions
A flag given '=value' raises BadOptionUsage
interfaces.signature: def _match_long_opt(self, opt: str, explicit_value: str | None, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_short_opt
interfaces.behavior: Iterates over the characters of a cluster like -abc. Each character is normalized and looked up in _short_opt. A value-taking option consumes the remainder of the cluster as its value (pushed onto rargs) and stops.
edge_cases: With ignore_unknown_options, unknown characters are collected and re-appended to largs as prefix+chars
Otherwise unknown raises NoSuchOption
interfaces.signature: def _match_short_opt(self, arg: str, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._get_value_from_state
interfaces.behavior: Gets the option value from rargs. If fewer than nargs remain: returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE when option.obj._flag_needs_value, else raises. For nargs==1 the next token is used, except that with _flag_needs_value a following token that looks like an option gives FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE. For nargs>1 returns a tuple and consumes nargs items.
edge_cases: Value tokens that start with a prefix are consumed as values for ordinary options
interfaces.signature: def _get_value_from_state(self, option_name: str, option: _Option, state: _ParsingState) -> str | cabc.Sequence[str] | T_UNSET | T_FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE

interfaces.name: _Option
interfaces.behavior: Holds the parsed option spec: _short_opts (prefix len 1 and name len 1), _long_opts (everything else), prefixes, dest, action (default 'store'), nargs, const, obj. takes_value is true for store and append. process(value, state) applies the action to state.opts and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: Unknown action raises ValueError('unknown action ...') at process time, not at construction
count starts from 0 and increments
append and append_const use setdefault lists
interfaces.signature: class _Option  # __init__(self, obj: CoreOption, opts: cabc.Sequence[str], dest: str | None, action: str | None=None, nargs: int=1, const: t.Any | None=None)

interfaces.name: _Option.process
interfaces.behavior: store sets opts[dest]=value; store_const sets const; append and append_const append to a list; count increments. Always appends obj to state.order, so repeated options are recorded repeatedly.
edge_cases: Unknown action raises ValueError
interfaces.signature: def process(self, value: t.Any, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _Argument.process
interfaces.behavior: For nargs>1: if all items are UNSET the value becomes UNSET, if only some are it raises BadArgumentUsage. An empty tuple becomes UNSET. Stores into state.opts[dest] and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: nargs=-1 with no values gives UNSET (not an empty tuple)
interfaces.signature: def process(self, value: str | cabc.Sequence[str | T_UNSET] | T_UNSET, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _ParsingState
interfaces.behavior: Holds mutable parse state: opts dict, largs (leftovers/positionals), rargs (remaining), order list.
interfaces.signature: class _ParsingState  # __init__(self, rargs: list[str])

interfaces.name: _unpack_args
interfaces.behavior: Distributes args across the nargs_spec. nargs==1 gives a str, nargs>1 gives a tuple, nargs<0 is a wildcard that takes the remainder. Specs after the wildcard are filled from the end, then reversed. Returns (tuple of values, leftover list). Missing values are UNSET.
edge_cases: Only one wildcard is allowed
Without a wildcard, excess args are returned as leftovers
interfaces.signature: def _unpack_args(args: cabc.Sequence[str], nargs_spec: cabc.Sequence[int]) -> tuple[cabc.Sequence[str | cabc.Sequence[str | T_UNSET] | T_UNSET], list[str]]

interfaces.name: _split_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns (prefix, rest). If the first char is alphanumeric the prefix is ''. If the first two chars are equal ('--') the prefix is two chars. Otherwise the prefix is one char.
edge_cases: An empty string gives ('', '')
interfaces.signature: def _split_opt(opt: str) -> tuple[str, str]

interfaces.name: _normalize_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns opt unchanged if ctx is None or has no token_normalize_func. Otherwise splits off the prefix and applies the function to the name only.
interfaces.signature: def _normalize_opt(opt: str, ctx: Context | None) -> str

interfaces.name: __getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Module-level deprecation shim. Names OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState return globals()['_<name>'] with a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel 2). split_arg_string is re-imported from shell_completion with a warning. Anything else raises AttributeError.
edge_cases: Other unknown names raise AttributeError(name)
interfaces.signature: def __getattr__(name: str) -> object

cards.error_conventions: Parse problems raise click.exceptions UsageError subclasses. NoSuchOption is for an unknown option (with a possibilities list for suggestions). BadOptionUsage(option_name, msg) covers a missing value, a value given to a flag, or a wrong nargs count. BadArgumentUsage covers a partially filled multi-value positional. Programmer errors use ValueError (invalid option prefix or unknown action) and TypeError (two nargs<0). Messages are gettext-wrapped (`_` and `ngettext`) and use repr-quoted names, e.g. "Option {name!r} requires an argument." / "Option {name!r} requires {nargs} arguments." / "Option {name!r} does not take a value." / "Argument {name!r} takes {nargs} values.". The ValueError and TypeError messages: "Invalid start character for option ({option})" is translated, "Cannot have two nargs < 0" is not.

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain pytest asserts. It checks private state (_opt_prefixes) directly on _OptionParser, both default and after Option.add_to_parser with custom prefixes '+' and '!'. It also has a parametrized test of shell_completion.split_arg_string. There are no direct tests of the parse_args error paths. Those are covered indirectly by the CliRunner-based tests for options and arguments elsewhere (not read).

extension_points.what_could_attach: Override in a Command subclass to return a customized _OptionParser (a subclass with different matching rules) or to pre-register extra options.

gaps.description: No abbreviation or prefix matching of long options (such as --verb for --verbose)
gaps.why_plausible: _match_long_opt does an exact dict lookup. NoSuchOption already gets the possibilities list, so a unique-prefix lookup would fit in the same place.

gaps.description: No 'extend' action and no per-option duplicate-use detection or error
gaps.why_plausible: The actions are a fixed set. Repeated store options silently overwrite, though state.order already records repeats.

gaps.description: No explicit '=' value support for short options (-o=val keeps '=' as part of the value)
gaps.why_plausible: Short-cluster handling just pushes the remainder of the cluster as the value.

gaps.description: Duplicate or conflicting option registration is not detected
gaps.why_plausible: add_option silently overwrites existing entries in the dict.

limitations: Module and class are internal and deprecated. _OptionParser is marked deprecated since 8.2 and slated for removal in 9.0, and the module docstring plans to remove more.
Only the actions store, store_const, append, append_const and count exist, and they are plain strings validated lazily.
Only one nargs=-1 positional is supported.
The parser does no type conversion, defaults or validation. Those live in core.
Argument parsing is two-phase: all options are processed before positional assignment, so positional nargs cannot influence option parsing.
parse_args mutates the input list.
Tests for this module are minimal; direct unit coverage of parsing behavior is thin.

cards.summary: src/click/shell_completion.py implements Click's shell completion. shell_complete() parses an instruction such as "bash_source" or "zsh_complete" from an env var. It looks up a ShellComplete subclass in the `_available_shells` registry. It then either prints the shell script (`source`) or the formatted completions (`complete`). Completion resolves a Context chain from the already-typed args (`_resolve_context`), picks the object that completes the incomplete word (`_resolve_incomplete`), and calls that object's `shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`. That call returns a list of CompletionItem. Each shell subclass supplies a script template (`source_template`), env-var parsing (`get_completion_args`) and an output wire format (`format_completion`). Wire formats: bash and fish use "type,value" lines (fish adds a tab and help), while zsh and powershell use 3-line "type\nvalue\nhelp" records with "_" as the no-help sentinel. Custom shells can be registered with add_completion_class.

interfaces.name: shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Entry point (line 19). Splits `instruction` with partition('_') into shell and instruction. Looks up the class with get_completion_class, instantiates it as comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var), and returns 0 or 1. 'source' echoes comp.source() as encoded bytes with nl=False. 'complete' echoes comp.complete() as encoded bytes, with a trailing newline. Bytes are written so Windows does not turn LF into CRLF.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns 1
Unknown instruction returns 1
Instruction without '_' gives shell=whole string and instruction='' so it returns 1 (or 1 for unknown shell)
The shell name is the part before the first underscore, so registered names containing '_' can never match
interfaces.signature: def shell_complete(cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, complete_var: str, instruction: str) -> t.Literal[0, 1]

interfaces.name: CompletionItem
interfaces.behavior: Generic class with __slots__ value, type, help, _info (line 67). Defaults: type='plain', help=None. Extra **kwargs are kept in _info and read as attributes through __getattr__.
edge_cases: Unknown attribute returns None instead of raising AttributeError
type values the built-in shell scripts handle: plain, dir, file; any other type is ignored by the bash, fish and powershell scripts
interfaces.signature: class CompletionItem(t.Generic[_ValueT_co])  # __init__(self, value: _ValueT_co, type: str='plain', help: str | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any)

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Returns self._info.get(name), so missing metadata is None (line 100).
edge_cases: Only called for attributes not found normally
interfaces.signature: def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: ShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: Base class (line 277, versionadded 8.0). Holds cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var. Subclasses must set the class vars `name` and `source_template`.
edge_cases: get_completion_args and format_completion are abstract and raise NotImplementedError in the base class
The base class can be used directly to call get_completions (tests do this)
interfaces.signature: class ShellComplete  # __init__(self, cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, complete_var: str)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Stores cli, ctx_args (a mutable mapping), prog_name and complete_var (line 306).
edge_cases: ctx_args is later mutated by _resolve_context, which sets resilient_parsing=True
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, complete_var: str) -> None

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.func_name
interfaces.behavior: Property (line 318). Replaces '-' with '_' in prog_name, strips non-word ASCII characters with re.sub(r'\W*', '', flags=re.ASCII), and returns f'_{safe}_completion'.
edge_cases: A prog_name with only symbols gives '__completion'
interfaces.signature: def func_name(self) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
interfaces.behavior: Returns the dict used to format source_template (line 326), with keys complete_func (func_name), complete_var and prog_name.
edge_cases: Subclasses can add keys, though the _SourceVarsDict TypedDict only declares three
interfaces.signature: def source_vars(self) -> _SourceVarsDict

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Returns source_template % source_vars() (line 338).
edge_cases: A literal '%' in a custom template must be written as '%%', otherwise the formatting fails
The result is encoded and written without a trailing newline by shell_complete
interfaces.signature: def source(self) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 346). Must return (args, incomplete) read from env vars.
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_args(self) -> tuple[list[str], str]

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
interfaces.behavior: Line 353. Calls _resolve_context, then _resolve_incomplete, then obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete). Returns a list of CompletionItem.
edge_cases: Empty incomplete is allowed
args may be mutated by _resolve_incomplete (an '--opt=value' split appends the option name)
interfaces.signature: def get_completions(self, args: list[str], incomplete: str) -> list[CompletionItem[str]]

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 367). Turns one CompletionItem into the shell wire string.
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[str]) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.complete
interfaces.behavior: Line 375. Calls get_completion_args, then get_completions, then format_completion on each item. Joins the results with '\n'.
edge_cases: No completions gives an empty string; shell_complete's echo then still adds a newline
The result has no trailing newline of its own, since echo adds one
interfaces.signature: def complete(self) -> str

interfaces.name: BashComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='bash', template _SOURCE_BASH (line 388). The script runs `env COMP_WORDS=... COMP_CWORD=... VAR=bash_complete $1`, then handles types: dir sets compopt -o dirnames, file sets compopt -o default, plain appends to COMPREPLY. The script registers with `complete -o nosort`, which needs Bash >= 4.4.
edge_cases: The bash script ignores item.help
interfaces.signature: class BashComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: BashComplete._check_version
interfaces.behavior: Static method (line 394). Finds bash with shutil.which and runs `bash --norc -c 'echo ${BASH_VERSION}'`. Prints a translated warning to stderr if the version is below 4.4, or if bash is not found or the version can't be parsed.
edge_cases: Never aborts; it only warns on stderr
The version comparison is done on strings, so '10' < '4' is True (a bug for major versions >= 10)
Tests monkeypatch it
interfaces.signature: def _check_version() -> None

interfaces.name: BashComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Calls _check_version(), then super().source() (line 427).
edge_cases: Runs a subprocess on every source call
interfaces.signature: def source(self) -> str

interfaces.name: BashComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Line 431. Splits env COMP_WORDS with split_arg_string. cword=int(env COMP_CWORD). args=cwords[1:cword]. incomplete=cwords[cword], or '' on IndexError.
edge_cases: A missing env var raises KeyError
A non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_args(self) -> tuple[list[str], str]

interfaces.name: BashComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Returns f'{type},{value}' (line 443). The help text is dropped.
edge_cases: A value containing a comma or newline is not escaped; the script does `IFS=',' read type value`, which keeps the rest of the line in value
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[t.Any]) -> str

interfaces.name: ZshComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='zsh', template _SOURCE_ZSH (line 447). The script uses _describe for items with help and compadd for items without. It is frozen for backwards compatibility, so changes go into format_completion.
interfaces.signature: class ZshComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 465. help_ = item.help or '_'. Escapes ':' as '\:' in the value only when help is present (not '_'). Returns 'type\nvalue\nhelp'.
edge_cases: A real help text of '_' is treated as no help
A multi-line help is not sanitized
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[str]) -> str

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same as BashComplete: COMP_WORDS and COMP_CWORD, args=cwords[1:cword] (line 453).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError
Non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_args(self) -> tuple[list[str], str]

interfaces.name: FishComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='fish', template _SOURCE_FISH (line 479). get_completion_args (line 485) reads COMP_WORDS (the whole command line) and COMP_CWORD (the current token, not an index). The incomplete word is split_arg_string(COMP_CWORD)[0] when non-empty. args=cwords[1:], and the last element is popped if it equals incomplete.
edge_cases: COMP_CWORD='' gives an empty incomplete
A quoted partial word is unquoted
A missing env var raises KeyError
interfaces.signature: class FishComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: FishComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 499. With help: 'type,value\thelp', where newlines in the help become literal backslash-n and tabs become spaces. Without help: 'type,value'.
edge_cases: An empty help string is treated as no help
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[str]) -> str

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='powershell', template _SOURCE_POWERSHELL (line 516, versionadded 8.5.0). The template uses Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native and parses the output 3 lines at a time. Types: plain gives a CompletionResult with a tooltip; dir and file use Get-ChildItem with a prefix glob.
edge_cases: The prefix for dir/file is wordToComplete+'*'
interfaces.signature: class PowerShellComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 537. Same 3-line format as zsh. Help has \r and \n replaced by spaces ('_' if no help). The value is not escaped.
edge_cases: CRLF becomes two spaces
A value containing a newline would break the framing
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[str]) -> str

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same logic as Bash and Zsh (line 525).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_args(self) -> tuple[list[str], str]

interfaces.name: add_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Registers cls in the module-level `_available_shells` under name or cls.name and returns cls, so it works as a decorator (line 560).
edge_cases: Overwrites an existing entry silently
No validation of the name
If name is None and the class has no `name` attribute, AttributeError is raised
interfaces.signature: def add_completion_class(cls: type[_ShellCompleteT], name: str | None=None) -> type[_ShellCompleteT]

interfaces.name: get_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Dict lookup in _available_shells (line 588). It has typing overloads for 'bash', 'fish' and 'zsh' only (no powershell overload).
edge_cases: Unknown name returns None
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_class(shell: str) -> type[ShellComplete] | None

interfaces.name: split_arg_string
interfaces.behavior: Line 598. A shlex.shlex posix=True, whitespace_split=True, commenters='' split. On ValueError (unclosed quote or trailing escape) it appends lex.token as the partial token. Moved here from parser in 8.2.
edge_cases: Unclosed quote keeps the partial token without the quote
Trailing backslash is dropped
Empty string gives []
interfaces.signature: def split_arg_string(string: str) -> list[str]

cards.error_conventions: The module has no custom exception types. shell_complete signals failure through a return code of 1, with no message. The bash version check prints translated messages to stderr with echo(err=True) and does not raise; the messages are sentences with no 'Error:' prefix. The abstract methods raise bare NotImplementedError. Bad environment variables (missing COMP_WORDS or COMP_CWORD, or a non-integer COMP_CWORD) surface as raw KeyError or ValueError from os.environ and int(). The completion code assumes make_context runs with resilient_parsing=True, so Click usage errors are suppressed during resolution.

examples.description: Base ShellComplete used to get completions directly in tests
Option name completion hides options already used
examples.code:
cli = Command("cli", params=[Option(["-t", "--test"])])
assert _get_words(cli, [], "-") == ["-t", "--test", "--help"]
assert _get_words(cli, ["-t", "a"], "-") == ["--help"]

examples.description: Registering a custom shell by decorator
Full complete via env var instruction
examples.code:
cli = Group("cli", commands=[Command("a"), Command("b", help="bee")])
env["_CLI_COMPLETE"] = f"{shell}_complete"
result = runner.invoke(cli, env=env)

examples.description: CompletionItem arbitrary metadata
examples.code:
c = CompletionItem("test", a=1)
assert c.a == 1
assert c.b is None

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain pytest asserts. Most tests call a local helper that builds ShellComplete(cli, {}, name, '_CLICK_COMPLETE') and compare the list of .value strings from get_completions. Cases covered: groups, chained groups, options, arguments, nargs, `--`, hidden params, Choice, Path and File types, and context_settings. The end-to-end tests use the `runner` fixture with env={'_CLI_COMPLETE': '<shell>_source|complete', COMP_WORDS, COMP_CWORD} and compare result.output exactly or by substring. BashComplete._check_version is monkeypatched out. Registry tests use a fixture that saves, clears and restores `_available_shells`. Other tests check the LF-only line endings of source output, zsh colon escaping, fish and PowerShell help escaping via format_completion, and no ResourceWarning from unclosed files. Some of these tests I saw only by name, not in full.

extension_points.name: ShellComplete.format_completion

extension_points.name: ShellComplete.get_completions

extension_points.name: CompletionItem type/kwargs
